You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Examine the encounter between Jesus and the Samaritan woman in John 4:5-42.

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** The meeting at Jacob's well in Sychar is one of the longest conversations in the Fourth Gospel. In it Jesus breaks social and religious barriers, reveals himself and gains a Samaritan following. An examination of the passage should deal with the setting, the dialogue and its meaning.

**1. The setting and the barriers broken.** Jesus is tired and sits by the well about noon (John 4:6). A woman comes alone to draw water. Several barriers are crossed: "Jews have no dealings with Samaritans" (John 4:9), because of old hostility over worship and race; Jewish teachers avoided speaking to women in public; and she may have been an outcast in her own town, coming at midday when others were not there. Jesus begins the conversation and asks her for a drink.

**2. The living water (John 4:10-15).** Jesus offers "living water", which will become in the believer a spring welling up to eternal life. The woman understands it literally, a convenient supply of water. The misunderstanding, common in John, leads to a deeper explanation: Jesus gives the life of the Spirit (compare John 7:37-39).

**3. Her life and the prophet (John 4:16-19).** Jesus asks her to call her husband and shows that he knows that she has had five husbands and now lives with a man who is not her husband. He does not condemn her but shows his insight, and she recognises him as a prophet.

**4. The true place of worship (John 4:20-24).** She raises the Samaritan and Jewish disagreement over Mount Gerizim and Jerusalem. Jesus says that the hour is coming, and now is, when true worshippers will worship the Father in spirit and truth, because God is spirit. Worship is no longer tied to one place but to the Spirit and to Jesus, who is the truth (John 14:6).

**5. The self-revelation (John 4:25-26).** When she mentions the coming Messiah, Jesus says, "I am he, the one who is speaking to you." This is the first open declaration of his identity in the Gospel, and it is made to a Samaritan woman.

**6. The woman as witness and the Samaritan mission (John 4:28-42).** She leaves her water jar, goes to the town and says, "Come, see a man who told me all that I ever did." Many Samaritans believe because of her word, and then more believe after staying two days with Jesus, saying that he is truly "the Saviour of the world". Meanwhile Jesus tells the disciples that his food is to do the will of the Father and speaks of the fields white for harvest (John 4:34-38).

**Conclusion.** The encounter shows Jesus offering the gift of the Spirit to the outcast, redefining true worship and revealing himself as the Messiah. It also shows the pattern of faith in John: from misunderstanding to witness to faith. The woman becomes an early missionary, and the story anticipates the spread of the Gospel beyond the Jews.
